papers.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.
papers.authors: Shinsei Ryu, Yu-ki Suzuki

papers.title: On-the-Fly Gaussian Process Reconstruction of the Galaxy Redshift Distribution for 3$\times$2pt Cosmology
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing, photometric galaxy clustering, and their cross-correlation, the so-called 3$\times$2pt analysis, is one of the primary probes Stage-IV surveys will use to constrain the dark-energy equation of state. Its accuracy depends critically on the calibration of the underlying photometric redshift distributions, $n(z)$, whose residual uncertainties can bias cosmological inference. However, conventional parametric nuisance models may not adequately capture the full range of plausible $n(z)$ uncertainties. We therefore present a cosmological inference framework that instead reconstructs $n(z)$ on the fly using Gaussian Processes (GPs), replacing per-bin shift-and-width parameterisations by a non-parametric, data-driven model. We validate the method on synthetic Euclid-like 3$\times$2pt data vectors representative of Euclid Data Release 1, sampling GP hyperparameters jointly with cosmological and nuisance parameters to reliably propagate $n(z)$ uncertainties into the posterior distributions. We find that the dependence of the inferred parameters on the adopted $n(z)$ model is markedly stronger in $w_0w_a$CDM than in $\Lambda$CDM. Opening the dark-energy sector both amplifies the biases induced by a given $n(z)$ treatment and changes which $n(z)$ reconstruction the data prefer, so that a model validated in $\Lambda$CDM does not automatically remain adequate once $w_0$ and $w_a$ are free. Our results thus indicate that Stage-IV surveys should define $n(z)$ uncertainty marginalisation requirements separately in cosmologies beyond $\Lambda$CDM to ensure unbiased dark-energy constraints.
papers.authors: Jip de Buck, Guadalupe Ca\~nas-Herrera, Henk Hoekstra, Angus H. Wright

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.
papers.authors: Sebastian Brezina, Martin Kr\v{s}\v{s}\'ak

papers.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.
papers.authors: Aditya Kumar Sharma, Alicia Calafat, Rodrigo Tenorio, David Keitel, Alicia M. Sintes

papers.title: The 21 cm-Lyman-$\alpha$ forest cross-power spectrum with a minimal effective field theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intensity maps of the 21 cm line and the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest trace the same cosmic volume at $2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$. Their cross-power spectrum is insensitive to foregrounds that do not correlate between the two probes and, together with the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, separates the mean 21 cm brightness temperature from the neutral hydrogen (HI) bias. Effective field theory models of each tracer exist, but at one loop they carry tens of nuisance parameters. We test whether a minimal effective field theory (mEFT), consisting of the tree-level Kaiser model with leading-order counterterms and stochastic terms, previously validated for the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, describes the 21 cm auto-, Ly$\alpha$ auto- and cross-power spectra jointly. We use the Sherwood 80 $h^{-1}$Mpc hydrodynamical simulation with HI painted onto halos at $z=2.4$-$4.2$, and reduce sample variance with Zel'dovich control variates. Each spectrum is validated separately and then in a joint fit with shared parameters. With scale cuts $k_{\rm max}=0.5$, $1.2$ and $2.0\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for the 21 cm auto-, cross- and Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectra, the mEFT fits all three spectra at all five redshifts. In the joint fit the mEFT determines the HI bias to 2.0-2.5% and the Ly$\alpha$ density bias to 2.1-2.3%. The scale cuts follow the HI velocity dispersion and the Ly$\alpha$ pressure-smoothing scale. When the brightness temperature is left free, the fits that include the cross-spectrum prefer values 20-30% above the true one, at 1-2$\sigma$, while the two auto-spectra together do not constrain it. A prior on the HI bias recovers the true value of the brightness temperature.
papers.authors: G. Autieri, V. Ir\v{s}i\v{c}, M. Viel

papers.title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, with their equilibrium chiral magnetic effect, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants. Previous results are brought to common conventions, with hypotheses stated and notions defined. New results: the characterization of the operators whose covariant symbol is gauge-field independent and the ordering independence of the integrated anomaly; the anomaly factorization on a closed four-manifold without the homotopy hypothesis, the factorization into instanton number and $N_3$ holding exactly when the untwisted index vanishes; the Luttinger--Ward identity behind the renormalized-velocity current and the continuum conditions replacing the compactness of the Brillouin zone in the non-renormalization theorems; the identification of the Moyal $N_3$ of the chiral separation effect with the fibre degree of the principal symbol; the residue evaluation of the Fermi-surface invariant of the non-elliptic models, in the continuum and on a lattice, and the equilibrium current of the conserved charge along the magnetic field that it implies -- a chiral magnetic effect permitted by the non-Hamiltonian form of these models -- which the model with spherical Fermi surfaces trades for a chiral separation effect and a single-Weyl anomaly, and a modification of it restores at the price of the anomaly; and the index-pairing form of the chiral separation invariant.
papers.authors: M. A. Zubkov

papers.title: Parallel alignment of radio AGN jets and large cosmic web structures in the direction of the Shapley supercluster
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aims. We investigated the potential large-scale alignment of radio active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets in the proximity of the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) area and its correlation with the identified cosmic web structures. Methods. We analyzed 28 radio AGNs divided into two populations with comparable sky coverage north and south of a diffuse X-ray filamentary structure connecting clusters in the SSC core. We measured the average jet position angles (PAs) and combined them with spectroscopic redshifts to assess the persistence of the alignment along the line of sight. Results. We detected a significant large-scale alignment of the radio AGN jets with the foreground X-ray filament (oriented at PA $\sim$ 115$^\circ$ $\pm$ 10$^\circ$). Both the northern (PA $\sim$ 117$^\circ$) and southern (PA $\sim$ 129$^\circ$) groups align with this axis, yielding an overall statistical significance of 4.5 $\sigma$ (upper and lower bounds: 6.1$\sigma$, 3.8 $\sigma$). Although the projected alignment is highly significant, sparse spectroscopic coverage (seven sources spanning 0.048 $\lesssim$ z $\lesssim$ 0.55) suggests that this spatial coherence may extend beyond the SSC (z $\sim$ 0.048), hinting at a line-of-sight correlation across significantly larger cosmic scales. Conclusions. The observed alignment cannot be explained by localized dynamical processes alone. These findings may indicate a persistent influence of the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, or preferred directions of matter collapse, on supermassive black hole spin axes, highlighting a connection between AGN jet morphology and the underlying dark matter distribution. Such alignments represent an important systematic that must be accounted for in precision cosmology with surveys such as Euclid.
papers.authors: I. Baronchelli, T. Venturi, V. Casasola, P. Merluzzi, C. Burigana, G. Busarello, M. Bonato, O. Smirnov, T. Ronconi, M. Massardi, E. Liuzzo

papers.title: Shedding light on modified recombination scenarios with Rayleigh scattering of the CMB
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rayleigh scattering (RS) of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons by neutral hydrogen and helium, during and shortly after the last scattering surface, adds a frequency-dependent contribution to the CMB anisotropies that scales approximately as $\nu^4$ at leading order. The RS signal is most relevant at $200\,{\rm GHz}\lesssim\nu\lesssim800\,{\rm GHz}$ and could be detected using future CMB experiments. Because RS acts in a frequency-dependent manner which is sensitive to the ionisation history of the cosmological recombination process, it provides an additional probe of the recombination history. This makes it a natural test of modified recombination scenarios, such as variable electron mass $m_{\rm e}$ or fine-structure constant $\alpha$, which have been proposed to ease the Hubble tension. The correlation between the RS and primary CMB signal, both in temperature and polarisation, further enhances its usefulness for constraining cosmological parameters. Using a multi-frequency Fisher analysis with realistic noise and foregrounds, we forecast parameter constraints and biases for PICO and LiteBIRD + Planck. For PICO, adding RS improves the $\Lambda$CDM constraints on cosmological parameters by $\lesssim7\%$, but improves the constraints on some parameters ($H_0$, $m_{\rm e}$, $\alpha$, $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$, $\Omega_{\rm c}h^2$) by $\simeq31\%$ for some modified scenarios in the recombination history. However, the improvement for LiteBIRD + Planck is limited to less than $2\%$ for most of the parameters. Neglecting RS biases the cosmological parameters by up to $\simeq1\sigma$ for PICO and below $1\sigma$ for LiteBIRD + Planck. Therefore RS must be modelled in the analyses of future CMB data.
papers.authors: Debabrata Adak, Elena Vanetti, R. T. G\'enova-Santos, Jens Chluba, Carlos Hern\'andez-Monteagudo, J. A. Rubi\~{n}o-Mart\'{\i}n

papers.title: Characterising a population of fast-declining SNe Ia in galaxy cluster cores
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galaxy cluster cores, characterised by old stellar population and suppressed star-formation are ideal for studying the environmental dependence of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). It is unclear whether the diversity of SNe Ia, parametrised by light curve stretch, stems from distinct explosion mechanisms or varying initial conditions, both closely tied to progenitor age. We analyse the light curve stretch and colour distribution of photometrically identified SNe Ia within the galaxy clusters cores, utilising the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) archival data. Using the AMPEL platform, we filter 89,025 ZTF transients spatially coincident with our galaxy cluster catalogues to identify 4,969 likely SN Ia candidates. We split this sample into three populations: core cluster SNe Ia $r \le 0.5R_{500}$, outer-core cluster SNe Ia $0.5R_{500}< r\le 2R_{500}$, and a reference population of non-cluster SN Ia. We present the largest sample of photometrically identified cluster SNe Ia to date, notably isolating a population of 242 SNe Ia within innermost cluster cores $r \le 0.5R_{500}$. This fast-declining SN Ia population is statistically different from the outer-core cluster and field SN Ia population at $\sim4\sigma$ level. A marginal statistical preference for a bimodal distribution over a unimodal one $\Delta AIC$ of 1.53 and 2.3 for each catalogue, indicate cluster cores almost entirely host fast-declining SNe Ia. Conversely, the colour distribution show no significant environmental variation. By filtering out the prompt SN Ia population, cluster cores provide an environment to directly probe the delayed SN Ia progenitor channel. Our observations support a two-population model where progenitor age drives the light curve stretch diversity. The low-stretch values observed in core cluster SNe Ia suggest sub-Chandrasekhar mass double degenerate systems as their likely progenitors.
papers.authors: A. Eranhalodi, J. Nordin, M. Kowalski, U. Burgaz, F. Fischer, M. Ginolin, Y. -L. Kim, T. E. M\"uller-Bravo, J. Sollerman, A. Townsend, A. Drake, M. Graham, D. Hale, J. C. Jaimes, R. R. Laher, J. Purdum

papers.title: Love numbers for the Myers-Perry geometry
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze Love numbers for scalar fields in the Myers-Perry geometry in arbitrary dimensions. The tidal responses of black holes are specified by two constants which encode a potential logarithmic running and the Love number. We argue that the parameter specifying the running is not sensitive to the structure of the horizon, and we explicitly compute this parameter for Myers-Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions by utilizing the asymptotic expansion of the wave equation. The Love numbers rely on the details of the boundary conditions at the horizon, and we compute them using several distinct approximations.
papers.authors: Rhucha Deshpande, Oleg Lunin

papers.title: Twisting IKKT with branes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the conjectural relationship between the IKKT matrix model and type IIB string theory, we classify supersymmetric twists of the matrix model, allowing for both dynamical and kinematical supercharges. Beyond the two twists available at any finite $N$, which we studied in our previous work, we find five additional classes at infinite rank which require non-commuting backgrounds associated with D-branes in IIB supergravity. Together, these twists realize representatives of every equivalence class of twisting supercharges in flat-space type IIB supergravity recently classified by the first author; however, the precise form of the orbit stratification differs. This difference is related to a higher central extension of the IIB superalgebra that appears in our treatment of the IKKT model in the BV formalism. Expanding around the non-commutative backgrounds gives worldvolume theories on products of A- and B-branes, including four-dimensional BF theory on an emergent D3-brane. We relate all these twists to deformations of BCOV theory (the closed string field theory of the topological B-model) using the open-closed duality of classical string field theory. For one of the twists with Spin$(7)$ symmetry, we also show the localization of the IKKT partition function by Moore, Nekrasov, and Shatashvili can be directly reconstructed with the BV formalism, with their auxiliary field completion encoded by quadratic antifield terms. Throughout, we provide self-contained treatments of the formal techniques we employ.
papers.authors: Fabian Hahner, Natalie M. Paquette

papers.title: A precision bound for gravitational transseries
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose that the large $N$ transseries of a holographic observable above the black hole threshold admits a precision bound, a limit on how precisely the transseries can determine the observable at finite $N$, set by the data of its D-brane instanton sectors. In doing so, we develop methods in large $N$ resurgence, based on the work of \'{E}calle, that capture the $e^{-N^2}$ asymptotics of gravitational saddles beyond the $e^{-N}$ instantons. Under an assumption on the growth of the D-brane instanton sums that we expect in the black hole phase, we find an analytic obstruction to the resummation of the large $N$ transseries. This obstruction sets the precision bound. As our main example and consistency check, we study the $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and its black hole. We derive relations between the D-brane instanton data on thermal AdS and on the black hole, in the form of a duality that exchanges the numbers of D-brane instantons on the two backgrounds. In the index, these relations reproduce the actions of D3-branes wrapped on the black hole. We conclude with our expectations for generic situations and their relation to the double-cone wormhole.
papers.authors: Ji Hoon Lee

papers.title: The $(5,5)$ String
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an $N=(2,1)$ heterotic string with right-movers on $\mathbb R^{2,2}$ and left-movers of signature $(5,5)$, obtained by adjoining the lattice $\mathrm{II}_{3,3}$. Unlike the standard $N=(2,1)$ strings it requires no null current, and its target space remains four-dimensional. All of its states, an infinite tower with sixteen supercharges, are massless. For the neutral bosons, the Kutasov-Martinec determinant action is dual to a cubic action for a self-dual metric coupled to self-dual Maxwell fields, and we complete it with fermions using a single superfield. For the charged states we give evidence that the couplings are the structure constants of a Lie superalgebra formed by the physical states of the left-movers. We are thus led to propose that the classical target theory is a self-dual gauge theory for this superalgebra: every state of the string is a gauge field, and gravity is part of the gauge algebra. This would be a purely cubic field theory of all the modes of a closed string.
papers.authors: Justin Kaidi

papers.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$\alpha$ Forest at the Field Level
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.
papers.authors: Divij Sharma, Roger de Belsunce, Mikhail M. Ivanov

papers.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.
papers.authors: Sergio Sanjurjo, Themistocles Zikopoulos

papers.title: Decoupling Dynamics: A Tale of Two Limits
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.17327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The symmetries of a $d$-dimensional QFT are known to be captured by a topological theory in one dimension higher, the Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which is invariant under gauging finite symmetries of the QFT, but not under dynamical gauging of continuous symmetries. We show that the distinct SymTFTs of a $d$-dimensional QFT before and after dynamical gauging of a continuous Abelian symmetry arise as different topological limits of the same dynamical holographic gauge theory in $(d+1)$-dimensions. Gauging changes the boundary condition of this dynamical theory and thereby selects a different topological limit, explaining why the associated SymTFT changes. We give a fully quantum definition of these SymTFTs at the level of Hilbert spaces and operators by combining suitable limits of the bulk holographic theory with photon truncation. This construction clarifies how topological symmetry defects, charges, and anomalies survive while the dynamical information carried by currents is discarded. We study non-anomalous and anomalous examples, providing a complete quantum analysis for $(2+1)$-dimensional bulks. For a four-dimensional boundary theory with a mixed axial-vector anomaly, we recover the SymTFT of the non-invertible chiral symmetry that remains after gauging the vector symmetry.
papers.authors: Andrea Antinucci, Oscar Lewis
